name: Slack Green tests
ownerWords: and how has the a/b tests going in general? what worked/didn't work? did anything work at all?  your duty is to check ab test results as they clear every day. NEVER CHANGE SHIT UNLESS PROVEN!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
goal: Every Slack Green A/B test gets its call on the day it clears, and nothing reaches all users unless its test proved it (c222). PostHog project 226805 is the only list of tests, read fresh each run: a test is live while its experiment has a start date and no end date, and every test, in the browser or in the worker, sends the $feature_flag_called exposure with an sg-exp- flag key (slack-green CLAUDE.md, A/B tests). The call is recorded in PostHog as the experiment's end date and conclusion. Its read date is the 'Read date: YYYY-MM-DD' first line of the experiment description, else 28 days after its start.

metrics.label: Slack Green tests past their read date with no recorded call
sg-exp- flags with exposures in the last 14 days and no PostHog experiment
PostHog reads that failed in this check

onMiss: source_errors: fix the precheck or POSTHOG_PERSONAL_API_KEY in slack-green scripts/seo-agent/.env first. Then make one call for each overdue_test slice. Read the experiment's description for its primary metric and PostHog's result for that metric, from POST /api/projects/226805/query/ with {"query": {"kind": "ExperimentQuery", "experiment_id": <id>, "metric": <that entry of the experiment's metrics>}}; the slice's counts (first exposure, signup or connect within 7 days, paid within 28 days, QA people removed, the ab-results-page method) and Fisher p are a cross-check. won: the test arm beats control on the primary metric with p under 0.05, or at a read date set before launch PostHog shows the test arm at 95% or more chance to beat control. lost: the same proof with control ahead. flat: neither, which includes a test too small to tell; it ends on control. Every PostHog read and write here runs on us-metal02 against https://us.posthog.com with the header 'Authorization: Bearer <POSTHOG_EXPERIMENTS_API_KEY>', the key in ~/Documents/Github/slack-green/scripts/seo-agent/.env that has experiment and feature flag write. Record the call with PATCH /api/projects/226805/experiments/<id>/ with end_date now, conclusion won, lost or inconclusive, and conclusion_comment as one line with the arms' numbers and p. Then apply it: lost or flat sets the flag to control at 100%, won sets the test arm to 100%, with PATCH /api/projects/226805/feature_flags/<flag id>/. Server-side tests in the slack-green proxy ignore the flag, so open one slack-green PR that removes the lost arm or keeps the won arm as the only path, run its scoped checks, merge it yourself with `bash <(git show origin/main:scripts/merge-pr.sh) <pr>` (c74 pre-approves merges until launch, c214), and walk the result on prod. Never put a merge on For you. Before a flat call, read PostHog's result beside the slice's Fisher p: when either reading is under 0.05 and the test has no pre-set read date, do not end it; write a 'Read date:' line 14 days out in its description with the numbers and let it run. A test whose flag got no new exposure for 14 days or more lost its code path, so it cannot run on: record it with conclusion stopped_early and a comment naming the replacing change and both readings, and change nothing for users. A test may move its read date only when its description names a planned sample it has not reached: write a new 'Read date:' line with the reason, once per test. After a call, follow any 'Holdout after the read' note in that experiment's description: build and launch the 50/50 holdout it names, with its own experiment and a 'Read date:' line, unless the call shipped what the note says makes it moot. Each untracked_test slice is a live test with no experiment: with the same key, POST /api/projects/226805/experiments/ with feature_flag_key the slice's flag, name the flag key, start_date its first exposure, and a description whose first line is 'Read date: YYYY-MM-DD', 28 days after the first exposure unless the test's PR or code comment names another, then read it like any test. Never change anything for all users without a won call, and never email users. Report each call in one short line, like 'sg-exp-x lost: control 4 of 106, test 1 of 111, p 0.2, flag back to control'. With nothing overdue, end with no message.
